event: Palantir Technologies UK, Ltd. (company 07042994) incorporated.
notes: Companies House register. Registered office now Birchin Court, London EC3V 9DU.

event: Government Digital Service contract for an "Enterprise Analytical Platform and Intelligence Service" with Palantir.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2015-09-01; GDS; "Palantir"). Value as published: £734,834.

event: MoD software licence for a data-science decision-support pilot for naval personnel management.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2018-05-11; MINISTRY OF DEFENCE; "Software Licence PT-SOL-LEV2").

event: Louis Mosley, then described as Palantir's UK boss, hosts a dinner attended by NHS England chair David Prior, the eve of NHSX's launch, at which future uses of NHS data were discussed; Mosley follows up by email.
notes: From emails released to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism under FOI. NHSX said Palantir secured no work as a result of a separate Oct 2019 meeting with NHSX chief Matthew Gould.

event: NHS England contracts Palantir (with Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Faculty) for the NHS Covid-19 Data Store; Palantir's initial fee is £1.
notes: Mosley told MPs in July 2025 the £1 charge was needed to put Palantir 'on a payment system' and 'was really a token' (https://committees.parliament.uk/oralevidence/16290/html/, Q107). The March 2020 contract value is not in contracts.csv.

event: MoD awards Palantir "Provision of Data Integration Services" via the G-Cloud 12 framework.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2020-04-23; MINISTRY OF DEFENCE; "Provision of Data Integration Services").

event: Government publishes the Covid data store contracts, including Palantir's, hours before proceedings brought by openDemocracy and Foxglove were due to start.
notes: As reported by Digital Health (30 Mar 2021).

event: Palantir's Covid data store work extended: DHSC "Provision of Palantir Foundry Services" and an NHS Arden & GEM CSU G-Cloud trial purchase for the Covid response.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2020-06-12; Department of Health and Social Care; "Provision of Palantir Foundry Services"). Also Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2020-06-12; NHS ARDEN AND GREATER EAST MIDLANDS COMMISSIONING SUPPORT UNIT; "Provision of Data Management Platform"). (https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/c66036ee-a63e-4452-bafe-2410e9b51587). Digital Health reports a four-month extension "at a cost of £1million".

event: Crown Commercial Service contract for a "Foundry Data Connector" technical feasibility evaluation (used for the Cabinet Office border-flow programme).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2020-08-31; Crown Commercial Service; "Provision of a Foundry Data Connector - Technical Feasibility Evaluation (TFE)"). Link to the border-flow programme is Louis Mosley's account to MPs (Q119), who said the contract expired in 2024 and the data and logic were exported 'seamlessly'.

event: NHS England awards Palantir a two-year contract to continue Foundry for the Covid-19 Data Store (to Dec 2022), via G-Cloud 11 without a published tender.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2020-12-11; NHS ARDEN AND GREATER EAST MIDLANDS COMMISSIONING SUPPORT UNIT; "National Health Service Commissioning Board and National Health Service Trust Development Authority: Provision of Data Management Platform Services"). Reported at the time as £23m (The Register, https://www.theregister.com/2020/12/21/nhs_awards_23m_twoyear_deal/).

event: openDemocracy, backed by Foxglove, files for judicial review of the December 2020 Palantir data deal, arguing it reached beyond Covid and required consultation and a fresh DPIA.

Foxglove and openDemocracy say the government has committed not to extend Palantir's contract beyond Covid uses without public consultation; NHS England denies conceding and says the claimants dropped the case.
notes: Both sides' positions given in the source.

event: Internal email from Louis Mosley titled 'Buying our way in…!' discusses 'hoovering up' NHS suppliers (later reported by Bloomberg).
notes: Bloomberg report dated 30 Sep 2022; quoted wording via Liberty Investigates. A Palantir spokesperson called the language 'regrettable'. Mosley said in Aug 2026 it was 'a thought experiment about a potential strategy which we never pursued'.

event: MoD awards Palantir "Data Integration and Management" call-off via G-Cloud 12.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2022-03-03; Ministry of Defence; "703156450-Data Integration and Management").

event: DLUHC contract for a Ukrainian humanitarian relief case management system (published value £0).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2022-03-08; DEPARTMENT FOR LEVELLING UP, HOUSING AND COMMUNITIES; "Ukrainian Humanitarian Relief Case Management System").

event: NHS England publishes its planning notice for an NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP).
notes: Find a Tender record ocds-h6vhtk-0328ce (sources/raw/find-a-tender/).

event: NHS England extends the Palantir Foundry "Data Platform Service" to 11 June 2023 to support the FDP procurement, saying a change of contractor now would be "impractical and uneconomic".
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2022-08-25; NHS England; "Contract Extension of the Data Platform Services").

event: DLUHC "Palantir Foundry Enterprise" software-as-a-service contract.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2022-09-22; DEPARTMENT FOR LEVELLING UP, HOUSING AND COMMUNITIES; "Palantir Foundry Enterprise").

event: MoD signs a three-year Enterprise Agreement for Palantir software "at all security classifications" (1 Dec 2022 to 30 Nov 2025).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2022-11-25; MINISTRY OF DEFENCE; "Palantir Technologies UK Ltd / UK MoD Enterprise Agreement").

event: NHS England issues the FDP and Associated Services tender: five-year value "up to £360,000,000", up to £480m with extensions.
notes: Tender release 000669-2023 in the Find a Tender record.

event: Peter Thiel tells the Oxford Union 'the NHS makes people sick' and that Britain has a 'Stockholm syndrome' about it, answering a question that referred to Palantir's pursuit of the NHS data contract.
notes: Oxford Union's own video; see data/quotes.json. Louis Mosley later told MPs Thiel was 'speaking in an entirely personal capacity'.

event: NHS England awards Palantir a 12-month "Palantir Foundry Transition & Exit Contract" to move Covid-era products to the new FDP supplier.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2023-06-09; NHS England; "Palantir Foundry Transition & Exit Contract"). See data/sovereignty-notes.md.

event: Alex Karp, on BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, says 'That data belongs to the government of the UK' and acknowledges joined-up FDP data could be sold in future by a government, 'not by me'.
notes: Digital Health also reports a YouGov poll for the Doctors' Association finding 48% of adults would likely opt out if a private company ran the FDP.

event: A separate NHS Privacy Enhancing Technology contract (reported at £35m) goes to IQVIA after NHS England split the FDP programme on data-safeguarding grounds.
notes: Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee report HC 61, para 86. Not in contracts.csv.

event: NHS England signs the FDP contract with a Palantir-led consortium (with Accenture, PwC, Carnall Farrar and NECS); the award was announced in November 2023 and the contract formally began in March 2024.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2023-12-22; NHS England; "Federated Data Platform and Associated Services"). Find a Tender gives contract signature 22 Nov 2023 and value £182,242,760, "not a committed amount", forecast up to £330m. Start date and consortium from NHS England (https://www.england.nhs.uk/digitaltechnology/nhs-federated-data-platform/security-privacy/contract-explainer/).

event: Before Christmas, NHS England publishes a heavily redacted version of the FDP contract, including most of the "protection of personal data" section.
Good Law Project sends NHS England a pre-action letter saying the redactions mean the public is 'unable properly to understand or scrutinise' how personal data will be handled.
notes: NHS England republished the contracts with fewer redactions in March 2024 (same source).

event: NHS England republishes the FDP contracts with fewer redactions following the Good Law Project warning.
Hundreds of NHS workers blockade the entrance to NHS England's London headquarters calling for the Palantir contract to be cancelled.
notes: PA report syndicated by LBC (July 2025).

event: Northumbria Healthcare NHS FT buys Foundry support for the Supply Chain FDP product.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2024-09-20; NORTHUMBRIA HEALTHCARE NHS FOUNDATION TRUST; "Foundry Support for Supply Chain FDP").

event: FOI correspondence shows Palantir held talks with the Ministry of Justice about using its technology to calculate prisoners' "reoffending risks" and lobbied new ministers.
Louis Mosley's witness statement to the UK Covid-19 Inquiry urges government to invest in a 'Common Operating System' spanning local and central government and healthcare, as broad as possible.
notes: Inquiry document INQ000536417, published March 2025.

event: Coventry City Council awards a "Strategic AI Platform" contract to Palantir (2025 to 2030).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2025-01-30; COVENTRY CITY COUNCIL; "COV - 21614 - Strategic AI Platform"). Published value £500,000; the Guardian reports it as £500,000 a year.

event: Prime Minister Keir Starmer visits Palantir's Washington office after meeting President Trump; Louis Mosley meets him there.
notes: Mosley told MPs the visit 'was done through the proper channels' and was not arranged by Peter Mandelson (https://committees.parliament.uk/oralevidence/16290/html/, Q141-142).

event: Palantir tells investors Q4 international revenue growth was driven 'in large part by the U.K., including our work with the NHS', with 87 acute trusts and 28 integrated care boards signed up to the FDP as of Nov 2024.
notes: Earnings-call transcript (chief revenue officer Ryan Taylor). On the same call Karp said Palantir is here to "scare enemies and, on occasion, kill them".

event: BMA annual representative meeting passes a motion that Palantir is 'an unacceptable choice of partner' for the FDP.
notes: Motion quoted to Louis Mosley by Dr Lauren Sullivan MP, Q127 ("last month"). Mosley replied the BMA had "chosen ideology over patient interest".

event: Liberty Investigates and i report a police pilot dubbed 'Nectar' (Project Nectar): Palantir working with Bedfordshire Police, Hertfordshire and Cambridgeshire on a 'real-time data-sharing network', with data drawn from nine forces initially, and a Leicestershire-led East Midlands project covering five forces.
notes: Based on FOI documents from Bedfordshire Police; the forces aim to apply it nationally.

event: Louis Mosley and NHS England give evidence to the Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee on Palantir, the FDP and lock-in. NHS England says about 69% of trusts have implemented the FDP and that the NHS's Foresight AI study has been paused pending advice to the Information Commissioner.
notes: Corrected figure (69%) is the witness's own clarification in the transcript.

event: Coventry City Council's Palantir AI contract draws union concern; on 2 Sept the council's leadership announces a review after protests over Palantir's links to the Israel Defense Forces.
notes: First reported 30 Aug 2025 (https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/aug/30/coventry-city-council-signs-ai-deal-contract-palantir-technologies).

event: MoD and Palantir sign a strategic partnership: up to £1.5bn of Palantir investment, London as its European defence HQ, up to 350 jobs, and defence opportunities "worth up to £750 million over the next five years", including targeting and "kill chain" capabilities.
notes: The release says the work will ensure "data remains sovereign". Not a contract award; no row in contracts.csv.

event: Louis Mosley says Palantir will not bid for the government's planned digital ID scheme, calling it a programme to be decided "at the ballot box, not in the company boardroom".
notes: Times Radio interview as reported by Liberty Investigates (12 Nov 2025).

event: MoD direct-awards Palantir a follow-on Enterprise Agreement under Procurement Act 2023 s41 (no competition for technical reasons; disproportionate technical difficulty of changing supplier). Contract signed 30 Dec 2025, running 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2029.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2025-12-17; Ministry of Defence; "MOD Palantir Enterprise Agreement"). Value £240,600,000 inc. VAT as published. See data/sovereignty-notes.md.

event: MPs raise concerns about UK Palantir contracts after a Swiss investigation (WAV/Republik) into the suitability and security of its products.
Green Party leader Zack Polanski stages a protest at Palantir's London office, pinning a 'dismissal letter' to the door.
notes: Louis Mosley's own account at a Centre for Policy Studies event (CapX video, Apr 2026).

event: Metropolitan Police buys licences and services to trial Palantir Foundry, initially for professional-standards work (Unified Data Platform Phase 1, 1 Feb to 30 Apr 2026).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2026-01-30; METROPOLITAN POLICE SERVICE; "Unified Data Platform Phase 1"). MOPAC later found this trial was directly awarded without advertising (Novara Media, 21 May 2026).

event: Financial Conduct Authority awards Palantir an "Enterprise Search Decision Intelligence" proof of concept (30 Jan to 29 May 2026).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2026-01-30; Financial Conduct Authority; "Enterprise Search Decision Intelligence PoC").

event: Opposition politicians call for Palantir contracts to be halted over transparency and Peter Mandelson's lobbying firm Global Counsel; the Information Commissioner is investigating Foreign Office and DHSC refusals to release information, including official FDP reports.
notes: ICO matter concerns FOI refusals, not a data breach.

event: Guardian reveals a 2025 Department of Health briefing for Wes Streeting warning that Palantir's reputation would hinder the FDP rollout.
notes: BMA GP committee deputy chair Dr David Wrigley is quoted saying members could refuse to use parts of the system.

event: Palantir announces it has moved its headquarters from Denver to Miami.

MoD answers a written question (PQ 111951) confirming the Enterprise Agreement was direct-awarded under Procurement Act 2023 s41, Schedule 5 paras 6 and 7, and that the decision was the Defence Secretary's.
notes: Asked by Martin Wrigley MP, answered by Luke Pollard MP.

event: The Met confirms it is using Palantir AI to analyse internal data on sickness, absences and overtime to identify professional-standards concerns; the Police Federation calls it "automated suspicion".
Early Day Motion 2868 'Palantir and the NHS' tabled, condemning DHSC over lack of transparency on the FDP award and calling for British-based alternatives.
notes: Tabled by Helen Morgan MP; 60 signatures per beyondthevote.co.uk (refreshed 7 Sep 2026).

event: Guardian reports the FCA has given Palantir access to its internal intelligence "data lake" for a three-month financial-crime trial.
notes: Corresponds to the 30 Jan 2026 FCA proof of concept in contracts.csv.

event: Financial Times reports ministers have taken soundings on triggering the FDP break clause when it becomes available in 2027; officials argue running the FDP could be transferred to another provider.
notes: As reported by the Guardian (31 Mar 2026), which quotes Louis Mosley urging ministers not to give in to 'ideologically motivated campaigners'.

event: Guardian reports Palantir staff working on the FDP were given NHS.net email accounts, SharePoint and Teams access.

Westminster Hall debate on the FDP; Labour and Lib Dem MPs call for the contract to be scrapped. Health minister Zubir Ahmed says 'who contracts with the FDP will be open to question as we go forward'.
notes: Minister quoted on NHS England's FDP contract explainer; MPs' calls reported by the Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/apr/16/labour-and-lib-dem-mps-demand-shameful-palantir-nhs-contract-be-scrapped).

event: Palantir posts 'The Technological Republic, in brief', a 22-point summary of Karp and Zamiska's book, on X; UK MPs call it 'the ramblings of a supervillain'.
notes: MP reaction: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/apr/21/palantir-manifesto-uk-contract-fears-mps

event: Two petitions calling for the government to end Palantir contracts (all public contracts; the NHS FDP contract) pass 229,000 signatures combined.
notes: Petition figures as reported; petitions not opened directly.

event: Financial Times reports NHS England allowed Palantir and other contractor staff access to identifiable patient data in part of the FDP before pseudonymisation; Louis Mosley calls it 'a specific technical permission inside one staging environment'.
notes: Guardian (11 May 2026) reporting the FT; Mosley response as quoted in the Commons committee report (https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/53352/documents/298462/default/).

event: King's Speech includes legislation for the NHS Single Patient Record.
notes: Cited in Commons committee report HC 61, para 91.

event: Deputy Mayor for Policing and Crime refuses approval for the Met's proposed two-year Palantir 'Unified Operational Analytics' contract (reported as £50m), citing a 'clear and serious breach' of procurement rules and value for money; the mayor's spokesperson also cites firms who 'act contrary to London's values'.
notes: LGL gives £25.3m in 2026/27 plus an optional £24.8m one-year extension. First reported by the Guardian on 21 May (https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/may/21/london-mayor-sadiq-khan-blocks-met-police-deal-with-palantir). Not in contracts.csv (no award).

event: NFLMS replacement: BlueLight Commercial, for Police Digital Service, publishes a contract award notice to Palantir for the National Firearms Licensing Management System (decided, contract pending; 4 Sep 2026 to 3 Sep 2031).
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2026-05-21; POLICE DIGITAL SERVICE; "BLC0222 - National Firearms Licensing Management System (NFLMS)"). Value £9,000,000 inc. VAT as published.

event: Palantir sends MOPAC a pre-action letter and then files a High Court claim alleging the decision was influenced by its values and ethics.
notes: Guardian 9 Jun 2026 (pre-action letter, first reported by the Times); claim filed in June per the Guardian 14 Oct 2026.

event: Martin Wrigley MP warns the US CLOUD Act may apply to Palantir's FCA work; the FCA trial is at its 12-week stage.
notes: See data/sovereignty-notes.md.

event: Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee report 'Rewiring the state' calls Palantir's presence 'an unacceptable point of weakness' and recommends exercising the February 2027 FDP break clause and publishing a costed exit plan by end-2026.
notes: HC 61 (2026-27), recommendations 95-98, including setting out why the £240m MoD contract was awarded without competition. Good Law Project says more than 79,000 supporters have joined its campaign against Palantir in the NHS (https://goodlawproject.org/mps-call-for-government-to-kick-palantir-out-of-the-nhs/).

event: London Assembly Police and Crime Committee questions the Deputy Mayor for Policing and Crime on the blocked Palantir deal.
Mayor's office grants the Met a 12-month extension to its Palantir pilot while the force procures a long-term supplier.
notes: Extension value not given in the source; not in contracts.csv.

event: Commons Health and Social Care Committee urges the government to end the Palantir FDP contract and find a replacement, citing 'serious mistrust' among the public and the medical profession.
notes: Second Commons committee to do so.

event: Guardian reports Palantir paid about £2m UK corporation tax for 2024 despite large public-sector contracts.
notes: See data/tax.csv (2024 current UK corporation tax £1,352,787; total tax charge £2,079,242).

event: NESO direct-awards Palantir an "Interim Capability" contract for Connections and Skip Rates work on Foundry (8 Sep 2026 to 31 Jul 2027) while a competitive procurement is run.
notes: Matches data/contracts.csv row (awarded 2026-08-25; NATIONAL ENERGY SYSTEM OPERATOR LIMITED; "NESO Interim Capability"). Value £21,240,324 inc. VAT as published. Justification quoted in data/sovereignty-notes.md.

event: High Court told Sadiq Khan has agreed to have his texts and emails searched in Palantir's claim against MOPAC.
Palantir appoints former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson as a senior vice-president alongside Louis Mosley.
More than 44,000 people have filed formal data-protection objections asking NHS England to stop their data being used in the FDP.
notes: Objections are under data protection law; NHS England must stop unless it shows a "compelling reason" (per the source).

event: National Data Guardian Dr Nicola Byrne urges ministers to give substantial weight to the 'trust factor' in deciding the FDP contract's future, citing reluctance among local organisations to adopt it.
notes: As reported by the Guardian (17 Oct 2026, "this week").

event: FCA says it has not renewed its short-term contract with Palantir.
notes: Headline report only; the FCA statement itself was not opened.

event: Palantir Technologies UK files 2025 accounts: turnover £262.5m (UK £236.4m), profit before tax £25.1m.
notes: Figures from data/tax.csv.

event: Palantir and MOPAC settle the High Court claim: both withdraw allegations and bear their own costs; MOPAC says its decision 'was not based on Palantir’s values or ethics' and that Palantir may bid in the Met's new procurement.
notes: Joint statement as quoted by the JC; trial had been due in January 2027 (City AM, https://www.cityam.com/?p=2465877). JC reports the case is understood to have cost the taxpayer up to £3.3m.

event: FOI responses gathered by Medact show 16 NHS trusts and health boards say they do not use the FDP; Greater Manchester's care board calls it "duplicative" and "retrograde".
notes: The Guardian notes the government faces a decision on the break clause.

event: End of the initial three-year committed term of the FDP contract; the government must decide whether to extend (break clause) by then.
notes: Date from Commons committee report HC 61 para 86. NHS England says only three years are committed, extendable by 2+1+1 years to a potential end in March 2031 (https://www.england.nhs.uk/digitaltechnology/nhs-federated-data-platform/security-privacy/contract-explainer/).
